name: dsp_export
title: Export a DSP script as a plugin for other DAWs: a CLAP file, or C++ source.
description: Export a DSP script as a plugin for other DAWs: a CLAP file, or C++ source. format clap (the default): copies the platform's script player and embeds the script in its trailer (Linux/Windows) or bundle resource (macOS, re-signed ad hoc with the system codesign tool). The copy is a plugin of its own, under the script's id and name, that plays this version of the script in any CLAP host (it reads no library), written to <folder>/<plugin name>.clap (default: the script's folder, under export/) with the licenses to ship beside it (notices). It runs on this platform, as fast as the player it copies (a debug build's is slow). format source: a C++ project of the plugin template that builds the same plugin (same id, parameters and state) as CLAP and VST3, plus AU on macOS, with the script compiled as C++, written to the empty <folder> (default: the script's folder, under export/<script>-source); its README says how to build it, and license (MIT unless GPL-3.0-or-later) is the license of its own files. Export again after changing the script; an export does not follow the library. See describe for errors and examples.

format.description: clap (default): a plugin file; source: a C++ project

folder.description: an absolute folder to write to (for clap, ~/.clap installs it for this user); for source, empty or new

license.description: source: the license of the project's own files (default MIT)

path.description: the plugin file, or the project's folder

player.description: clap: the script player it was copied from

notices.description: clap: the licenses to ship with the plugin

name: dsp_preview
title: Draw a plugin's editor to a PNG, after a test signal plays through it.
description: Draw a plugin's editor to a PNG, after a test signal plays through it. Give plugin (an id) or script (a name in the library). A fresh instance, set by patch (a merge patch) when given, plays signal -- an effect: sine (the default, at frequency_hz), sweep, impulse, noise or silence, peaking at level_db; an instrument: notes (the default), note or silence -- for seconds while its editor watches, so meters and the script's draw() show what played. Then the editor is drawn without a window, scale times its design size, and saved as a PNG (path; width and height in pixels): read the file to see it. A script with neither editor() nor draw() shows the automatic editor. pointer, if given, acts on the editor first, in its design units (the picture's pixels at scale 1): move (a hover; a drag after a press), press, release, click, double_click, drag (from x, y to to_x, to_y) and wheel (steps notches, up positive), with shift, ctrl or alt held; edits is a merge patch of what they changed, as a user's edits would. problems says what went wrong in the editor's code (a loop stopped by its budget, an index out of range), with the line. Headless pictures use EGL on Linux, Metal on macOS and WGL on Windows; an unavailable renderer returns dsp.no_picture. See describe for errors and examples.

level_db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (dB; accepts quantity strings)

frequency_hz.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (Hz; accepts quantity strings)

x.description: design units: the picture's pixels at scale 1

y.description: design units: the picture's pixels at scale 1

edits.description: what pointer changed, as a merge patch

name: dsp_test
title: Play test signals or notes through a plugin and measure it: levels, THD, pitch.
description: Play test signals or notes through a plugin and measure it: levels, THD, pitch. Give plugin (an id: a script's, or any effect's or instrument's) or script (a name in the library). A fresh instance, set by patch (a merge patch) when given, plays each signal. An effect: sine (frequency_hz; gain_db and thd_percent), sweep (20 Hz to 20 kHz), impulse (response_db at octave centres), pink noise and silence, each peaking at level_db. An instrument, at velocity 0.8: notes (a note, then a chord), note (A4; pitch_hz, the pitch heard), and silence (no notes); release_ms is how long the sound lasts after the last release. Each reports peak and RMS in dBFS, DC, samples beyond 0 dBFS and denormals; problems says in words what looks wrong (clipping, DC, sound from silence, no output, a note out of tune, sound that never dies away, non-finite samples the framework silenced, a script stopped by its loop budget or indexing outside an array). cpu_percent is measured, so it varies between runs. save: true keeps each output as a WAV (path) for analyze and compare. automation is a list of {param, at_s, value}: semantic patch keys and physical values, as discrete sample-accurate changes applied to every signal (no implicit ramps). automation.max_step is the largest adjacent-sample change in full-scale amplitude; baseline_max_step uses the same render without automation; excess_step is their positive difference. A step above both four times baseline and 0.05 suggests clicks or zipper noise: a screening heuristic, not proof of an artifact or of inaudibility. sidechain supplies a timed key; its middle half is measured against a connected silent key with identical automation: gain_change_db is negative for ducking, null if either output is below -120 dBFS. Slow attack may not settle in that window. Each pass has a fresh instance and initial patch. THD and impulse response are omitted during automation or a non-silent key; gain_db then describes the changing render, not static gain. notes supplies an instrument's sequence ({key, velocity, start_s, length_s}), replacing the notes signal; defaults become notes and silence. Do not combine it with the A4 note signal or select only silence. release_ms starts at its last note-off. Times round to samples at the render rate; spans must fit within seconds. See describe for errors and examples.

signals.description: default: effects five; instruments three, or notes and silence with custom notes

value.description: physical value, enum key or boolean

automation.description: discrete physical-value changes on every signal

level_db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server.

frequency_hz.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server.

notes.description: instrument sequence replacing the notes stimulus

level_db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (dB; accepts quantity strings)

frequency_hz.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (Hz; accepts quantity strings)

gain_db.description: sine: the fundamental out against in

pitch_hz.description: note: the pitch heard (A4 is 440 Hz)

release_ms.description: an instrument's: sound after the last release

name: dsp_write
title: Save a DSP script to the library and compile it, with diagnostics.
description: Save a DSP script to the library and compile it, with diagnostics. Writes <library>/<name>/<name>.cpp (replacing it), compiles it and returns the compiler's diagnostics, each with a hint. A script that compiles becomes a plugin of the script player under the id its Info gives: plugin.list shows it (listed) and fx.add loads it. Instances already playing it pick up the change within half a second, crossfaded; one that fails to compile leaves them playing the old code. Language: the dsp-language guide. See describe for errors and examples.

name.description: the script's folder and file name

kind.description: effect (audio in, audio out) or instrument (notes in)
audio (a sample) or impulse (a Convolver's response)

files.description: the script's files (AudioFile, Convolver), when it has any: give each an absolute path in a patch, {"properties": {"<key>": "/path.wav"}}

listed.description: plugin.list shows it (the script player is on the plugin path)

name: engine_devices
title: List native audio device names, host APIs, rates and channel capacities.
description: List native audio device names, host APIs, rates and channel capacities. Enumerates PortAudio devices on macOS/Windows without opening a stream. backend defaults to portaudio; dummy returns an empty list without initializing hardware. Use exact host_api and name values with engine.start. Linux uses JACK ports and returns backend.unsupported; engine.inputs lists running JACK inputs. See describe for errors and examples.

name: engine_inputs
title: The device inputs a track can record: audio channels and MIDI devices.
description: The device inputs a track can record: audio channels and MIDI devices. audio: one entry per input channel (channel, the 1-based number track.set record_input takes, and the device port it is connected to). midi: the MIDI devices (names track.set record_midi matches; JACK ports or native CoreMIDI/WinMM inputs, fixed until restart). While the engine is stopped: running false and empty lists (engine.start opens the device). See describe for errors and examples.

name: engine_start
title: Start playback through JACK, native PortAudio, or a device-free dummy.
description: Start playback through JACK, native PortAudio, or a device-free dummy. backend: jack (Linux default), portaudio (macOS/Windows native device), or dummy (default elsewhere, no device). For portaudio, host_api, input_device and output_device select exact names from engine.devices. inputs defaults to 0 (playback only); outputs defaults to 2. rate defaults to the project rate. PortAudio opens up to 16 native MIDI inputs; engine.inputs lists their names. Dummy is paced like a device. block: the device block in frames (default 256); the device's period may differ and is reported. anticipative (default true): render ahead of the playhead on worker threads (edits are heard up to 200 ms later); false renders everything in the audio callback. The engine runs at the device's rate (media is resampled; renders stay at the project's rate). Background and live thread capacities follows the app's Audio processing threads preference (Automatic by default); live helpers join each callback with no added latency. memory_lock reports the default-off host-process memory policy: requested, active, and a structured OS error on failure. cpu_idle_latency reports the default-off 20 microsecond PM QoS request, released on engine stop. A protection failure does not prevent audio startup. MIDI inputs that refuse to open are skipped: midi_warnings reports each device, numeric os_error, message and corrective hint; audio continues. See describe for errors and examples.

name: engine_status
title: Real-time engine state: backend, rate, block, device period, latency, xruns.
description: Real-time engine state: backend, rate, block, device period, latency, xruns. plan_latency: the session's plugin delay in frames; device_latency: frames from the engine's outputs to the device. restart_needed: the device changed rate or went away; engine.stop and engine.start again. midi_devices_changed is advisory: MIDI topology changed but audio keeps running. midi_devices_message asks for an explicit engine restart to pick up the new set; existing port names stay fixed. midi_dropped: native MIDI messages/packets rejected or lost to bounded queues (zero for other backends). midi_warnings lists inputs skipped at start, with device, numeric os_error, message and corrective hint. meter_drops: entries a full ring dropped (the renderer's, the audio callback's) — a strip's peak/RMS missed a block, never audio. dropped/voice_dropped count lost plug-in output/voice records. memory_lock reports requested/active and an optional OS error with errno and a corrective hint, including while stopped. Bridges are excluded. cpu_idle_latency reports the owned 20 microsecond request with the same status/error fields; it affects system idle while held and leaves CPU frequency policy unchanged. live_helpers is the enabled live helper capacity. scheduling: each thread class's policy (none, normal, fifo, rr, high) and priority as applied at start: the device callback, live helpers, renderer and background helpers (real-time below a real-time callback when permitted). workgroup: whether the live helpers joined the device's audio workgroup (macOS CoreAudio; state none, ready, joined, partial or failed, with the helper counts and the last refusal's OS error, message and hint). warnings includes scheduling fallbacks and plan warnings with corrective actions. failed_errors adds structured code, message, path and hint to each failure. failed_fx: isolated plugins whose process crashed or hung (silent now; fx.restart re-creates them). See describe for errors and examples.

name: engine_stop
title: Stop real-time playback and release the audio device.
description: Stop real-time playback and release the audio device.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: env_add
title: Automate a parameter: a track's or route's mixer control, or a plugin's.
description: Automate a parameter: a track's or route's mixer control, or a plugin's. Target one of track (param volume|trim|pan|width|mute), route (volume|pan|mute) or fx (a semantic key such as "gain" or "filter1.cutoff", or for other plugins a CLAP id or parameter name). points: [{beat|bar|seconds, value, shape?, tension?}]; values in the parameter's unit (dB, %, Hz… — text like "800 Hz" works for plugins); shapes linear, square, slow, fast_start, fast_end, bezier. Plugin values move along the parameter's curve (a log cutoff sweeps evenly in pitch). take (param volume|pan|mute): a take envelope, its points in beats from the item's start (it moves with the item); it shapes the take after its take FX (a MIDI take needs an instrument in its take FX). See describe for errors and examples.

name: env_list
title: List envelopes (optionally of one track, route or plugin).
description: List envelopes (optionally of one track, route or plugin).  See describe for errors and examples.

name: env_points_set
title: Replace an envelope's points (all of them, or those in a beat range).
description: Replace an envelope's points (all of them, or those in a beat range). from_beat/to_beat: replace only points with from_beat <= beat < to_beat. See describe for errors and examples.

name: env_remove
title: Remove an envelope (the parameter returns to its set value).
description: Remove an envelope (the parameter returns to its set value).  See describe for errors and examples.

name: env_set
title: Set an envelope's options: active (heard), mode (read, touch, latch, write).
description: Set an envelope's options: active (heard), mode (read, touch, latch, write). visible shows or hides the envelope's lane in the arrange view (a hidden envelope still plays while active). See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_add
title: Insert a plugin into a track's (or a take's) FX chain and return its id.
description: Insert a plugin into a track's (or a take's) FX chain and return its id. plugin: id or name from plugin.list; patch: an initial (partial) patch for semantic plugins. chain: main (default; the track's effects) or input (the recorded-input chain). take instead of track: the take's own chain (take FX) — the item plays through it before the track's input, cut to the item; an instrument there plays a MIDI take on its own. An instrument with outputs past its main pair (a multi-out sampler's Kick, Snare...) gets that many more channels on the track, and its pins.out sends each output there; route.matrix lists them and route.add {channels: {from: [3, 4]}} sends one to a buss. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_chain_delete
title: Delete a saved FX chain preset by name.
description: Delete a saved FX chain preset by name. Removes the preset file from the user's chains directory. Tracks that loaded it keep their effects. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_chain_list
title: List saved FX chain presets by name, path and effect count.
description: List saved FX chain presets by name, path and effect count. Lists valid supple.fx-chain/1.0 files, sorted by name and path. Invalid documents are skipped with warnings. See fx.chain.save and fx.chain.load. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_chain_load
title: Append or replace a track's FX chain from a preset in one undo step.
description: Append or replace a track's FX chain from a preset in one undo step. Give exactly one of name (in the user's chains directory) or path (relative to the work directory). mode defaults to append; replace removes the target chain, its envelopes and key routes. Validates every plugin and state before changing the model. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_chain_save
title: Save an ordered FX chain as a named preset.
description: Save an ordered FX chain as a named preset. Save main (default) or input FX to the user's chains directory. Preserves semantic patches or opaque base64 state. Refuses empty chains; replace: true explicitly overwrites an existing name. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_copy
title: Copy a plugin and its current settings into a track's FX chain.
description: Copy a plugin and its current settings into a track's FX chain. Adds a new instance of fx's plugin to track's main (default) or input chain, at index (default: the end), with the source's options (label, bypass, offline, wet, isolation, oversampling, parallel, pdc) and its settings as they are now: the running plugin's own state when the engine has one (editor edits included), else the model's patch or state. Not copied: envelopes, key routes into the source, and, when the track differs, channel pins. The source stays where it is; use fx.move to move it. One undo step. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_describe
title: Describe an instance and its live problems; full adds parameters and patch.
description: Describe an instance and its live problems; full adds parameters and patch.  See describe for errors and examples.

filter.description: Plain parameters only: list those whose name contains this text (case-insensitive).

status_available.description: A live instance supplied its current problems

problems.description: Current plugin problems: code, message, scope, line when known, hint, silent; scope host when unreadable

sidechain_channels.description: The plug-in's key input: route.add {fx} feeds it

latency_samples.description: The instance's reported latency, in samples

params_total.description: Plain parameters matching; at most 512 are listed.

name: fx_learn_list
title: List the MIDI controller bindings of plugin parameters.
description: List the MIDI controller bindings of plugin parameters. Every effect's, or one effect's (fx). control names the message in words. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_learn_remove
title: Remove a plugin parameter's MIDI controller binding.
description: Remove a plugin parameter's MIDI controller binding.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_learn_set
title: Let a MIDI controller (CC, note, pitch bend) move a plugin parameter.
description: Let a MIDI controller (CC, note, pitch bend) move a plugin parameter. One binding per parameter (a new one replaces it). midi.device: a substring of the MIDI input's name (empty: any). mode for a CC: absolute, relative1 (127 = -1, 1 = +1), relative2 (63 = -1, 65 = +1), relative3 (65 = -1, 1 = +1) or toggle (above 0 flips it). soft_takeover: an absolute control acts once it reaches the value. when_selected / when_focused / when_visible: only while the effect's track is selected, or its window or editor has the focus or shows (the GUI). See describe for errors and examples.

param.description: A semantic key, or a plain parameter's id or name (fx.describe)

name: fx_move
title: Move a plugin within a track chain or to another track.
description: Move a plugin within a track chain or to another track. Works on the track's chain, on its input chain (an input-chain effect stays on its track) and on a take's chain (take FX stay on their take: index only). See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_param_get
title: Read one saved plugin parameter by semantic key or numeric CLAP id.
description: Read one saved plugin parameter by semantic key or numeric CLAP id.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_param_set
title: Set semantic parameters in units, or plain plugin parameters by name/id.
description: Set semantic parameters in units, or plain plugin parameters by name/id. Plain CLAP/VST3 values use the declared range or plugin text; read-only parameters refuse edits. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_patch_get
title: Read a semantic plugin's saved patch.
description: Read a semantic plugin's saved patch.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_patch_list
title: List an instance's read-only factory patches, by name.
description: List an instance's read-only factory patches, by name.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_patch_merge
title: Merge a partial patch into a plugin instance; returns the effective change.
description: Merge a partial patch into a plugin instance; returns the effective change. Semantic plugins only. Values in physical units: {"params": {"gain": "-6 dB"}}. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_patch_set
title: Replace a semantic patch, or apply a factory patch by name.
description: Replace a semantic patch, or apply a factory patch by name. Give exactly one of patch or name. Factory names come from fx.patch.list; omitted parameters take defaults. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_remove
title: Remove a plugin instance (and its envelopes).
description: Remove a plugin instance (and its envelopes).  See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_restart
title: Re-create a plugin instance from its saved patch/state (after a crash).
description: Re-create a plugin instance from its saved patch/state (after a crash). engine.status lists failed_fx: isolated plugins whose process crashed or hung. The new instance starts from the model's patch or state. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_set
title: Set instance options: bypass, offline, wet (%), label, isolation, pins.
description: Set instance options: bypass, offline, wet (%), label, isolation, pins. isolation: in_process, dedicated (the plugin runs in a process of its own: a crash silences only it), shared_bridge (one process for all such plugins), inherit (the project default: in_process). pins: which of the track's channels (1-based; track.set channels adds 3-128) the plugin reads ({in: [l, r]}), writes ({out: [l, r]}) and keys from ({key: [3, 4]}: a detector on 3/4, for a plugin with a sidechain input); {} restores 1/2 in and out. out past its first two entries: a track channel for each of the plugin's auxiliary output channels in order (0: unconnected); fx.add sets them for a multi-out instrument. See describe for errors and examples.

wet.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (%; accepts quantity strings)

name: history_list
title: List the current branch's recent versions (newest first).
description: List the current branch's recent versions (newest first).  See describe for errors and examples.

name: history_redo
title: Redo the last undone change.
description: Redo the last undone change.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: history_undo
title: Undo the last change on the current branch.
description: Undo the last change on the current branch.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_add
title: Add an item on a track: MIDI written in notation, or an audio file.
description: Add an item on a track: MIDI written in notation, or an audio file. position in beats (quarter notes from the start) or bar (1-based). notation: e.g. "voice bass; 1: C2:q r:q C2:q r:q | F2:h G2:h" — every bar must add up; the item is as long as the written bars unless length (beats) is given. audio_file: a path at the project's sample rate; with the app's copy-imports setting on, the project keeps its own copy in its media folder. See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_apply-fx
title: Render an item through its take and track FX into a new audio take.
description: Render an item through its take and track FX into a new audio take. Renders the heard take alone (other items on the track silent) through its take FX and the track's main chain, before the fader and pan, over the item's span: MIDI becomes audio through the track's instrument. The file goes to the project's media folder. mode take: a new take, heard, beside the old one (MIDI stays a take). mode replace: the new take takes the old one's place. The item's fades and gain still apply when it plays; the track FX still process the result, so bypass or move them if they should not apply twice. See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_duplicate
title: Copy an item and its takes to a new beat position (default: immediately after).
description: Copy an item and its takes to a new beat position (default: immediately after).  See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_explode-takes
title: Spread an item's takes onto new tracks, or one after another on its track.
description: Spread an item's takes onto new tracks, or one after another on its track. In recording order. mode tracks: the first take stays on the item's track and each other take gets a new channel right below it (named after the take) at the same time. mode serial: the takes follow each other on the item's own track, each as long as the item. Every take becomes a one-take item with its FX and envelopes. See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_move
title: Move an item in time (position in beats or bar) and/or to another track.
description: Move an item in time (position in beats or bar) and/or to another track.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_paste
title: Copy items as they were in a version (a clipboard) to tracks and beats.
description: Copy items as they were in a version (a clipboard) to tracks and beats. version: where the items are read (default: now) — a GUI copy or cut remembers the version, so a paste reproduces the items as copied even after they were removed or edited. items: [{item, track, position}] (beats; channels only). Takes, fades, take FX and MIDI are copied; an audio source the project no longer has is restored. See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_remove

A locked item refuses every edit except {"locked": false}. timebase: what the item follows when the tempo changes — beats (moves and stretches with it), time (stays at its seconds), beats_position (its start follows the beat, its length stays in seconds) or track (inherit); the item keeps its place now. See describe for errors and examples.

locked.description: The arrange view marks locked items.

gain_db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (dB; accepts quantity strings)

Who did what: origin is gui, agent:<client>/<model>, mcp:<client>, lua:<script>, rpc. queries: include read-only commands (left out by default). since: only entries after this seq (poll with the last seq seen). origin: entries whose origin starts with this. The log keeps the last 2000 commands. See describe for errors and examples.

name: marker_list

name: marker_remove
title: Remove a ruler.
description: Remove a ruler.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: marker_set
title: Edit a ruler's position, name, or color.
description: Edit a ruler's position, name, or color.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: midi_edit
title: Edit a MIDI item's notes and CCs: add, remove, move, resize, velocity, quantize.
description: Edit a MIDI item's notes and CCs: add, remove, move, resize, velocity, quantize. ops run in order and are one undo step. notes: indices into midi.notes' list as it was before this command (every op refers to that list, so later ops are not affected by earlier removals). Beats are from the item's start. add {pitch, start, length, velocity?, channel?}; remove {notes}; move {notes, beats?, semitones?}; resize {notes, length? | length_delta? | start_delta?}; velocity {notes, velocity? and/or velocity_delta?}; quantize {notes? (all), grid (beats, on the project's grid), strength? 0-1, ends?}; cc.set {number, points [{beat, value}], channel?}; cc.clear {number, from?, to?}. Returns the new indices of the notes the ops added or changed (to keep a selection). See describe for errors and examples.

name: midi_get
title: Read an item's MIDI as notation.
description: Read an item's MIDI as notation.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: midi_notes
title: List a MIDI item's notes and CC points (beats from the item's start).
description: List a MIDI item's notes and CC points (beats from the item's start). Notes are in a fixed order (by start, then pitch); midi.edit refers to them by their position in this list. start/length/beat are in beats from the item's start; channel is 1-16 (omitted for 1). pooled: other items share this MIDI, and edits change them too. For writing whole phrases, midi.write with notation is usually better. See describe for errors and examples.

name: midi_write
title: Replace an item's MIDI with notation (the item keeps its position and length).
description: Replace an item's MIDI with notation (the item keeps its position and length).  See describe for errors and examples.

name: plugin_list

shadowed.description: Another location earlier on the plugin path has the same id; fx.add by id uses that one

name: plugin_scan
title: Rescan configured plugin paths and return the available plugins.
description: Rescan configured plugin paths and return the available plugins. wait: false scans in the background (every module through the supervised scanner) and returns at once with the current list and the scan's job; the catalogue changes when the job is done. A background scan already running is returned instead of a second one. See describe for errors and examples.

wait.description: false: scan in the background (default true)

name: project_get
title: Show the project: name, rate, tempo, meter, file, version and branch.
description: Show the project: name, rate, tempo, meter, file, version and branch. recoverable: recordings a crash left out of the project (project.recoverable). autosave_available: a newer autosave exists next to the file; open it as a project if you want it (nothing is loaded silently). See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_open

description: Open a project file (replaces the current project and its history). recoverable > 0: recordings a crash left out of the project; project.recoverable lists them and project.recover puts them back. autosave_available: a newer autosave exists next to the file (it is not loaded silently). See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_recover
title: Put recordings a crash left out back into the project (one undo step).
description: Put recordings a crash left out back into the project (one undo step). files: as project.recoverable lists them (omit for all). Each becomes an item on the track it was recorded on (or track) at the position it was recorded. See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_recoverable
title: List recordings a crash left out of the project.
description: List recordings a crash left out of the project. Takes recorded but never committed (the program stopped mid-recording) or never saved, found in the media folder's rec/. start_seconds is where each was recorded; seconds includes audio written after the file's last header update. See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_save
title: Save the project (canonical JSON) to its file or a new path.
description: Save the project (canonical JSON) to its file or a new path. path: where to save (becomes the project's file); omit to save in place. warnings: running plug-ins whose current state could not be read; the file keeps the state each had before (fx.restart, then save again, or replace the plug-in). See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_set
title: Change project metadata (name, title, author, notes, Console 9, timebase).
description: Change project metadata (name, title, author, notes, Console 9, timebase). timebase: what items follow when the tempo changes, for items and tracks that inherit it — beats (default), time or beats_position; they keep their place now. See describe for errors and examples.

history_budget_bytes.description: Estimated retained history byte budget; default 1 GiB. Leases and branch boundaries may exceed it.

name: project_template_delete

description: Delete a saved project template by name.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_template_list
title: List saved project templates by name and path.
description: List saved project templates by name and path.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_template_load
title: Start a new, unsaved project from a project template.
description: Start a new, unsaved project from a project template. Replaces the current project and its history, like project.new: unsaved changes are lost, so save first. The new project has no file until project.save {path} and gets its own copy of the template's audio; the template itself is never changed. See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_template_save
title: Save the whole project as a named project template.
description: Save the whole project as a named project template. Writes the project as it is now (tracks, FX and their states, routing, items, settings; not the history) to a folder of its own in the user's templates directory, with a copy of every audio file it uses. The project keeps its own file. replace: true replaces a template of that name. warnings: running plug-ins whose current state could not be read; the template has the state each had before. See describe for errors and examples.

The queued render is pinned to the session as it is now (its version; a branch's head when branch is given), so later edits do not change it; a dry run lists its files now. The queue is transport-like state: not an undo step, not saved with the project. See describe for errors and examples.

name: render_queue_list
title: The queued renders, in the order render.queue.run runs them.

name: route_add
title: Send one track to another track, bus, the master, or a plug-in's key.
description: Send one track to another track, bus, the master, or a plug-in's key. The destination must not feed the source. Master accepts routes. With fx instead of to, the send feeds that plug-in's sidechain (key) input — e.g. a kick keying a compressor on the bass; it is delay-compensated, and soloing the keyed track does not stop the key. Hardware routing is not supported yet. See describe for errors and examples.

fx.description: Feed this plug-in's sidechain (key) input instead of a track's input; `to` may be left out

volume_db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (dB; accepts quantity strings)

oneOf.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server.

mono.description: Sum the source to mono before the pan

channels.title: channel_map
channels.description: Which source channel feeds which destination channel, pair by pair: {from: [1, 2], to: [2, 1]} swaps, {from: [1, 1], to: [1, 2]} sends the left channel to both, {from: [], to: []} restores the identity

name: route_list
title: List sends with endpoints and mixer settings.
description: List sends with endpoints and mixer settings.  See describe for errors and examples.

oneOf.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server.

name: route_matrix
title: What can be routed where: strips, plug-in keys, sends and blocked pairs.
description: What can be routed where: strips, plug-in keys, sends and blocked pairs. sources: strips in tree order (depth, parent, parent_send). destinations: strips and plug-in keys (fx with a sidechain input). A pair is blocked when the source's rule applies (masters feed only keys), the destination's rule applies (channels take only hardware audio), it is the same strip, or it is listed in cycles (the destination already feeds the source). sends: existing routes per pair. Otherwise route.add accepts the pair. A source's channels past 2 are auxiliary (ADR-0020); channel_names names those a multi-out plug-in writes ({"3": "Kick"}), and route.add {channels: {from: [3, 4], to: [1, 2]}} sends that pair. See describe for errors and examples.

description: Describe the whole session in compact text (tracks, items, fx, routes). The quickest way to see where things are; use the IDs it shows with other commands. See describe for errors and examples.

name: take_activate
title: Choose the take heard from an item.
description: Choose the take heard from an item. take (its id) or index (0-based in the item's take order — the same position after item.split, which copies the takes in order: comping splits an item and picks a take by index on the piece). See describe for errors and examples.

name: take_add
title: Add a take to an item, optionally copied from another take of that item.
description: Add a take to an item, optionally copied from another take of that item.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: take_extract
title: Take a take out of its item into an item of its own on any channel.
description: Take a take out of its item into an item of its own on any channel. The new item copies the old one's length, fades, gain and timebase and starts at position (beats; default: where the item starts). The take keeps its FX and envelopes. The only take of an item moves the item itself. See describe for errors and examples.

name: take_list
title: List the takes of an item and identify its active take.
description: List the takes of an item and identify its active take.  See describe for errors and examples.

playrate.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server.

pitch.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server.

name: take_remove
title: Delete a take from its item (the item goes with its last take).
description: Delete a take from its item (the item goes with its last take). The take's FX, envelopes and unshared MIDI go with it. When it was the heard take, the next take is heard (else the previous one). item_removed: it was the item's only take, so the item was removed too. See describe for errors and examples.

name: take_set
title: Set take gain, pan, channel mode, name, source offset, or playrate and pitch.
description: Set take gain, pan, channel mode, name, source offset, or playrate and pitch.  See describe for errors and examples.

gain_db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (dB; accepts quantity strings)

pan.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (%; accepts quantity strings)

start_offset.description: Source position at the item start; negative for a late first pass.

playrate.description: Playback speed: 2 plays the source twice as fast. Its length in seconds is the item's, so the take runs out sooner or loops. Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (x; accepts quantity strings)

preserve_pitch.description: Keep the source's pitch when the playrate changes (the default). With pitch_mode "resample" the pitch follows the speed.

pitch.description: Pitch offset in semitones. Stretched when the pitch is preserved, otherwise a further speed factor of 2^(pitch/12). Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (st; accepts quantity strings)

name: tempo_set
title: Replace the tempo map: points {beat, bpm, ramp?}; the first must be at beat 0.
description: Replace the tempo map: points {beat, bpm, ramp?}; the first must be at beat 0. ramp: true changes the tempo linearly (in beats) to the next point; otherwise it steps. See describe for errors and examples.

bpm.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server.

name: time_convert
title: Convert a seconds, beat, or bar position to all three time domains.
description: Convert a seconds, beat, or bar position to all three time domains.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: timesig_remove
title: Remove the meter change at a bar: the meter before it continues.
description: Remove the meter change at a bar: the meter before it continues. Bar 1's meter cannot be removed (change it with timesig.set). See describe for errors and examples.

name: timesig_set
title: Set the meter from a bar on, e.g. {"bar": 9, "meter": "3/4"}.
description: Set the meter from a bar on, e.g. {"bar": 9, "meter": "3/4"}.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: track_add
title: Add a channel, buss or master strip and return its id.
description: Add a channel, buss or master strip and return its id. parent: a buss/master id (default tr_0); masters have no parent; index: position among its siblings; name: default the first free ch_N, buss_N or mstr_N. A new channel gets the user's default monitoring (on unless set otherwise; monitoring needs the track armed). See describe for errors and examples.

name: track_list
title: List tracks in tree order with their level, mute/solo, fx and items.
description: List tracks in tree order with their level, mute/solo, fx and items.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: track_move
title: Move a track under another track or reorder it among its siblings.
description: Move a track under another track or reorder it among its siblings. parent defaults to the track's current parent (a pure reorder); index defaults to the end of the destination's children. A track cannot move under itself or one of its own descendants. See describe for errors and examples.

name: track_remove
title: Remove a track with its items, fx, routes and envelopes (not a folder).
description: Remove a track with its items, fx, routes and envelopes (not a folder).  See describe for errors and examples.

name: track_set
title: Set track fields: name, type, volume, pan, mute, solo, polarity, mono, arming.
description: Set track fields: name, type, volume, pan, mute, solo, polarity, mono, arming. Only the given fields change. solo: off | on | in_place | defeat. armed + record_input (device input channels, 1-based) prepare a track for transport.record; record_midi records MIDI instead: a device name (substring of the MIDI port, "*" = every device) with midi_channel 1-16 (0 = all). monitor: off | on | auto (auto: while armed) — a monitored track hears its input live (an instrument plays the keyboard), also while stopped. record_mode: input (new items), midi_overdub (merge into the MIDI item under the start, as a new take), midi_replace. color: red | orange | yellow | green | teal | blue | violet | grey | "#rrggbb" ("" clears it), shown as a stripe on the track. See describe for errors and examples.

volume_db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (dB; accepts quantity strings)

pan.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (%; accepts quantity strings)

phase_invert.description: Flip the polarity of the main pair (after the FX chain, before the fader)

mono.description: Sum the main pair to mono (after the FX chain, before the fader and pan): a mono check on the master

parent_send.description: The implicit send to the parent buss/master (off: only explicit sends leave the strip)

timebase.description: What this channel's items follow when the tempo changes (those that inherit it): project, beats, time or beats_position; they keep their place now

channels.description: 1-2: the strip's main pair; up to 128 adds auxiliary channels 3-128 for routes and plug-in pins (a detector on 3/4, a multi-out instrument's outputs), outside the fader, pan and parent send

description: Add a strip from a track template (settings and FX) in one undo step. Give exactly one of name (in the user's track-templates directory) or path. parent defaults to the master. Every plugin and state is checked before the model changes. See describe for errors and examples.

title: Save a strip (settings and FX chains) as a named track template.
description: Save a strip (settings and FX chains) as a named track template. Writes a supple.track-template/1.0 file to the user's track-templates directory: the strip's type, name, colour, notes, level, pan and monitoring, and its main and input chains as fx.chain.save stores them (semantic patches or base64 state). Not routing or items. replace: true overwrites an existing name. See describe for errors and examples.

name: transport_get
title: The play position and whether it is playing.
description: The play position and whether it is playing.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: transport_loop
title: Set or toggle the loop range: playback reaching its end repeats it.
description: Set or toggle the loop range: playback reaching its end repeats it. start and end as seconds, beat or bar (start_bar 5, end_bar 9 = bars 5-8); a range turns the loop on unless enabled says otherwise; enabled alone toggles the current range. Recording while looping makes one take per pass on one item. Transport state: not an undo step, not saved in the project. See describe for errors and examples.

name: transport_metronome
title: Turn the metronome on or off and set its level; returns the settings.
description: Turn the metronome on or off and set its level; returns the settings. A click on every beat of the meter while the transport plays (the bar's first accented), in the live output only: renders and recordings never contain it. count_in_bars: that many bars of clicks (at the meter and tempo where playback starts) before transport.record begins — the position holds and nothing is recorded until the count ends; count_in_playback counts in before transport.play too. The count clicks even with the metronome off. Transport state: not an undo step, not saved in the project. No arguments: the current settings. See describe for errors and examples.

volume_db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (dB; accepts quantity strings)

name: transport_pause

description: Pause playback where it is (ends a recording).  See describe for errors and examples.

The recording keeps running; the committed items cover only the punch range (the file keeps everything). Not an undo step. See describe for errors and examples.

name: transport_seek

description: Stop playback and return to where it started (ends a recording).  See describe for errors and examples.
